screenSummary.playArea: A position-time graph with checkpoints a and b, their secant and a moving tangent, a speed graph below it, and the car on its road.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a route, drag the checkpoints, play or drag the time, mark a time, or reveal every match.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Find a time between the checkpoints when the car's speed equals its average speed.

screenSummary.playArea: A function graph with endpoints a and b, their secant and a tangent, and the graph of f′ below it.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a function, drag a and b, move x, and decide which hypothesis fails.
screenSummary.interactionHint: When can the theorem fail? Move a and b across a corner, a cusp, a jump or a pole.

lesson.moveCarHelp: Use Left and Right or A and D to move the car. Hold Shift for smaller steps.
lesson.close: Within 0.1 m/s at the marked time.
lesson.none: No c works on this interval.
lesson.conditions: The theorem needs f continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b).
lesson.challengePrompt: Mark a time when the speed equals the average speed.
lesson.near: A match lies within half a time step of the mark.
lesson.appliesExplanation: Both hypotheses hold on [a, b], so some c in (a, b) must have f′(c) equal to the secant slope.
lesson.continuityExplanation: f is not continuous at x = {{x}}, inside [a, b].
lesson.differentiabilityExplanation: f is continuous, but it has {{kind}} at x = {{x}}, inside (a, b), where f′ does not exist.
